#### Load Packages

```{r load-packages, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
```

**Load the data and provide a `glimpse()`**:

```{r data-1, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
music_data <- read.csv("data/mxmh_survey_results.csv")
glimpse(music_data)

```

# **Data Cleaning**

```{r}
# Showing which columns have null values and how many
music_data %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "na_count") %>%
  filter(na_count > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(na_count))

```

```{r}
# Summary to spot outliers
summary(music_data$Age)

# Count unrealistic ages
sum(music_data$Age < 10 | music_data$Age > 90, na.rm = TRUE)

# View rows with unrealistic ages
music_data %>% 
  filter(Age < 10 | Age > 90)
```

```{r}

# Checking that music hours per day doesn't contain unrealistic # of hours
summary(music_data$Hours.per.day)

music_data %>% 
  filter(Hours.per.day < 0 | Hours.per.day > 16)

# we will remove the 89 year old who listens to rap exclusively while working and has no perceived mental health issues

```

```{r}
cols <- c("Anxiety", "Depression", "Insomnia", "OCD")

# Checking if any values for self reported mental illness are out of the 0-10 range
music_data %>% 
  summarise(across(all_of(cols), 
                   ~ sum(. < 0 | . > 10, na.rm = TRUE)))


```

```{r}
yn_cols <- c(
  "While.working",
  "Instrumentalist",
  "Composer",
  "Exploratory",
  "Foreign.languages"
)

# Checking to see if any of the "yes" "no" columns have values outside of these options
sapply(music_data[yn_cols], function(x) all(x %in% c("Yes", "No")))

lapply(music_data[yn_cols], function(x) setdiff(unique(x), c("Yes", "No")))

sapply(music_data[yn_cols], function(x) sum(x == "", na.rm = TRUE))

# We will drop the rows that having missing values here, as there is no clear way how to impute them


```

```{r}
freq_cols <- c(
  "Frequency..Classical.",
  "Frequency..Country.",
  "Frequency..EDM.",
  "Frequency..Folk.",
  "Frequency..Gospel.",
  "Frequency..Hip.hop.",
  "Frequency..Jazz.",
  "Frequency..K.pop.",
  "Frequency..Latin.",
  "Frequency..Lofi.",
  "Frequency..Metal.",
  "Frequency..Pop.",
  "Frequency..R.B.",
  "Frequency..Rap.",
  "Frequency..Rock.",
  "Frequency..Video.game.music."
)

allowed_freq <- c("Never", "Rarely", "Sometimes", "Very frequently")


# Checking to see if any of the frequency columns have values outside of "Never, Rarely, Sometimes, Very frequently"
sapply(music_data[freq_cols], function(x) sum(!(x %in% allowed_freq)))
```

```{r}
# Cleaning our data

# dropping BPM column
music_data <- music_data %>% select(-any_of("BPM"))

# dropping 1 row that has a null value for Age
music_data <- music_data %>% 
  filter(!is.na(Age))

# Dropping the 89 year old year old who listens to only rap while working 24 hours a day(unrealistic value)
music_data <- music_data %>%
  filter(!(Age == 89 & Hours.per.day == 24))

# Dropping the rows that have non "yes" "no" answers for questions that only permit those values (9 rows were removed here)
allowed_yn <- c("Yes", "No")

music_data <- music_data %>%
  filter(
    if_all(all_of(yn_cols), ~ .x %in% allowed_yn)
  )

music_data_clean <- music_data

glimpse(music_data_clean)

```

# **Modeling**

```{r}
# Question 1: How does the number of hours spent listening to music per day vary by anxiety status and primary streaming service?

# factor the anxiety variable to have 3 levels (low, medium, high)
music_data_clean <- music_data_clean |>
  mutate(
    Anxiety_num = case_when(
      Anxiety <= 3 ~ 1,
      Anxiety <= 7 ~ 2,
      TRUE ~ 3
    ),
    Anxiety_cat = factor(
      Anxiety_num,
      levels = c(1, 2, 3),
      labels = c("Low", "Medium", "High")
    )
  )

# fit our linear regression model
model_rq1 <- lm(
Hours.per.day ~ Anxiety * Primary.streaming.service,
data = music_data_clean)

summary(model_rq1)





```
